acceptance: Decision gate (owner): choose per run between 'note and remove links' and 'regenerate the data'. Default if the owner has no preference: note and remove links. Regeneration of SF10 data is heavy work and needs the owner to name the run.
No dangling `datagen` symlink remains under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs` (`find . -maxdepth 3 -name datagen -type l ! -exec test -e {} \;` prints nothing).

Each of the three run folders in point 1 and `polars-version-matrix-20261120` holds a short `DATA-REMOVED.md` naming what was removed on 2026-11-22, why, the generating BenchBox commit where known, and the command that regenerates it.

Published or tracked analysis that cites these runs is checked: any document under `_project/analysis/` or the site that tells a reader to reuse those datagen folders is corrected or the item records that none exists.
Verification rubric: the find command output, the list of files added, and the grep used for the document check are pasted into context. Result JSON files are not edited.

Guardrails: never rewrite, move or delete a result file, manifest, log or qualification file; never recreate a link that points at the shared `datagen/` to make an old run look intact; host-local folders only, nothing from `benchmark_runs` is committed.
context: Origin: disk cleanup and root-cause review on 2026-11-22. The root volume fell to 46 GiB free, below the 50 GiB heavy-work floor. Cause found: generated benchmark data has no lifecycle (any session creates it under any run root, nothing removes it), and Time Machine local snapshots kept deleted data allocated. PR #4451 (https://github.com/BenchBox-dev/benchbox/pull/4451) added AGENTS.md [RUN-DATA-001] and made scripts/run_version_matrix.py delete its datagen/ and databases/ when a matrix completes.
description:
Problem: the 2026-11-22 cleanup removed generated data that finished runs still point at.

1. Seven `datagen` symlinks are dangling: `polars-2-1-spill-attribution-20261121/{2.0.0,2.1.0,q4-2.0.0-default,q4-2.1.0-budget4000}/datagen` (target `polars-version-matrix-20261120/datagen`), `polars-version-matrix-reference-20261119/{q41-1.44.2,q41-2.1.0}/datagen` (target that run's own `datagen`), and `duckdb2-followups/bb_2.0.0/datagen` (target `duckdb2-followups/bb_1.5.6/datagen`).
2. 145 result files in `polars-version-matrix-20261120/results` record `working_dir` under `polars-version-matrix-20261120/datagen/...`, which no longer exists. A few results in `dfprim` (12) and `q21-semi` (4) have the same kind of path.
3. `polars-version-matrix-20261120/matrix-manifest.json` pins four SF10 datagen manifest hashes; the data they describe (tpch, tpcds, ssb, clickbench at SF10) was deleted. The hashes were confirmed to match the data before deletion.

Nothing reads these paths today: `scripts/analyze_version_matrix.py` uses the manifest and result files only. The risk is a later rerun or audit that follows a link or path and silently regenerates different data, or concludes evidence was lost.

Expected outcome: each affected folder states plainly that its data was removed and how to regenerate it, and no dangling link remains.
